attribution.note: Marcus wrote this in his own Substack post as one of his points under 'In reality'. It is his assertion, not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: The normalised wording matches the statement: the LLM did not solve the problem alone and had a narrow, prescribed role inside a larger system. It is a factual claim about how the system was built.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: the LLM generates a designated part of a program, inside a search and evaluation process specified separately. The contract rightly does not stretch the claim to mean the LLM's contribution was trivial.

evidence.note: This is the original Nature paper (2023-12-14). It describes a supplied algorithm skeleton in which the LLM evolves only the 'priority' function, while separate evaluators run and score candidates and a programs database selects them. That meets the support condition.

reviews.rationale: The original paper shows the LLM working inside a human-supplied program skeleton, generating only the 'priority' function. Separate evaluators and a programs database score and select its outputs. The cap-set result therefore came from the full system, not from the LLM solving the problem end to end. This matches Marcus's description, and the packet contains no counterevidence.
